resources.string: Whitelister uses the AccessibilityService solely to detect when you are viewing Instagram Reels and prevent scrolling between them, helping you reduce time spent on Reels. All processing happens on your device; no data leaves the app.

Whitelister uses Android's AccessibilityService to interact with Instagram.

The service reads Instagram's on-screen interface — including the view structure and visible text such as account names and captions — but ONLY to detect when you are viewing Reels and to prevent scrolling between them.

All processing happens on your device. Nothing is stored, logged, or sent anywhere. Whitelister has no internet access, no analytics, and no ads.

By tapping "I Accept" you consent to the use of the AccessibilityService as described in our Privacy Policy.

Whitelister Privacy Policy

Whitelister is an Android app that helps you reduce time spent on Instagram Reels by using Android's AccessibilityService.

What data the AccessibilityService accesses
To function, Whitelister's AccessibilityService reads the on-screen user interface of Instagram (com.instagram.android), including the view hierarchy, view identifiers, and visible text such as account names and post captions. This access is required solely to detect when you are viewing Reels and to prevent scrolling between them.

How the data is used
All processing happens locally on your device, in memory, at the moment the screen is shown. Whitelister does not store, log, or transmit any of this information.

Data collection and sharing
Whitelister collects no personal data. It does not use the internet, contains no analytics SDKs, and displays no advertisements. No data is shared with the developer or any third party.

Your controls
You can disable the AccessibilityService at any time in Android Settings > Accessibility. Uninstalling the app removes all local preferences.

Contact
For questions, contact the developer via the project repository.
